title: Stand Firm and See the Salvation of the Lord
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: We are quick to doubt God when trouble comes, but we have something better than the Red Sea: the cross. Don't waste your suffering.
exhortation: God had just done miraculous things in Egypt. Pharaoh had set the Israelites free. Now Pharaoh's army is coming, and they're trapped in front of the Red Sea, and they cry out, "Is it because there are no graves in Egypt that you have taken us away to die in the wilderness?"

Think back on all God has done in your life. We're probably a little annoyed at the Israelites for doubting God. Didn't you just see his wondrous works? Didn't he just set you free from Egypt? And yet when pain and hardship come into our lives, we do the same thing. I find that's how it goes in my life. The car breaks down, I have a bad day at work, and I think, "Lord, what is going on?" We are so quick to doubt.

But we have something better than the miracles in Egypt and the parting of the Red Sea. We get to look back at the grace of God at the cross and see a loving Savior who gave everything and shed his own blood so that we might be redeemed. Won't he get us through a broken-down car?

And sometimes very hard things happen: cancer, the death of a loved one. I've been through a few things, and one phrase God gave me is this: don't waste your suffering. It is good to cry out to God in trials, but we can cry out in faith rather than fear and doubt. That helps open our eyes to what God is doing. Maybe he has put us in a hospital bed next to someone we're meant to be an example to and share the gospel with. Maybe the car broke down because the mechanic needs to hear the gospel. He is also doing something in our own hearts, exposing what needs to be exposed and showing us how faithful he is when times are hard. So don't waste your suffering. Look to God, and look to the ultimate proof that he is for us: the cross.
prayer: Lord, help us live with the confidence we should have as children of God. You will not abandon us or forsake us. Like the Israelites, we look back on trials and hardships in our lives and see your goodness and kindness through them.
But the Red Sea moment that shows most clearly that you will never forsake us is that you gave your Son. Thank you, Jesus. Thank you.
